candidate.explanation: v13 launch-hardening candidate, cut 2026-08-03 on branch v13 after SC-P0-01..06 and SC-P1-07,08,10,11,12 landed. It contains everything in the prior candidate a11afda PLUS: fail-closed entitlement so a transient Supabase failure can never read as 'Free' or create a duplicate checkout (271e31c), highest-valid-entitlement resolution across overlapping subscriptions (ebcfe5c), one server catalog deciding displayed AND charged currency with no silent cross-currency retry (6380016), production launch config that fails closed WITHOUT relying on a flag (6debd63), removal of the legacy client-email customer route and arbitrary portal returnUrl (77cee5b), react-router-dom 6.30.4 -> 7.18.2 with centralized internal-path validation (ca3eaa8), a zero-warning React correctness pass with a stale-response guard on every id-keyed studio loader (de9c779), typed error-to-copy states across billing/generation/export (f4394a9), sharper honest landing copy (45ec316), the billing state-contract matrix + trial-eligibility coverage (709015a), and the capped-beta value scorecard (879e1bb). Every automated check that can run without production secrets was re-run at this exact commit 5523187 on 2026-08-03. IMPORTANT: unlike the a11afda cut, the production configuration gate CANNOT be carried forward this time — SC-P0-04 changed backend/lib/launch-config.js by ~200 lines and backend/scripts/release-check.js, so the 2026-07-28 production /api/admin/readiness result no longer describes this candidate's config-gate code and must be re-observed against the deployed candidate. Documentation-only commits after this SHA (including this launch-state record) do not invalidate the candidate; anything under backend/, app-src/, app/, e2e/, api/ or config does.

blockers.title: react-router / react-router-dom 7.18.2 carry an open high advisory GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 (RSC-mode CSRF bypass)
blockers.closure: GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 is fixed only in react-router 8.3.0, which removes the react-router-dom package and requires React 19 / Vite 7 / Node >=22.22 — a stack upgrade beyond v13's scope. `npm audit --omit=dev` reports 2 high at 5523187. NOT reachable in practice: the advisory states it only affects applications using the unstable RSC APIs, and this app ships no RSC or SSR entry point (declarative BrowserRouter only). Close by either (a) owner accepting the risk with a named rationale and revisit date, or (b) upgrading to react-router 8 on a React 19 / Vite 7 migration. Until then it is an open, named, unreachable risk — it must not be reported as closed. Introduced alongside SC-P0-06 (ca3eaa8), which closed the three previously-open 6.30.4 advisories.
blockers.reachability_evidence: v14 SC-05 PROOF (imports/config, not prose): all 24 router imports in app-src resolve to 'react-router-dom' (zero from 'react-router/server' or any RSC entry); the app mounts a single declarative <BrowserRouter> in app-src/main.jsx; a grep for react-router/server, renderToPipeableStream, renderToReadableStream, react-server, RSC vite plugins, createStaticHandler and entry.server across app-src/api/vite config returns nothing; the build emits a pure client SPA (index.html + one client JS/CSS bundle, no server entry). The advisory applies only to applications using the unstable RSC APIs, which this build does not ship. `npm run audit` reports 2 high (react-router 7.12.0-8.2.0); the only fixes are a breaking downgrade to 7.11.0 or a react-router 8 / React 19 / Vite 7 migration — no safe forward patch on 7.x. Remains OPEN pending owner acceptance (named rationale + revisit) or the router-8 migration; not reachable, but not closed.

how_to_create_a_new_candidate: 1. Land all intended work on the release branch. No feature work after this point.
2. Set candidate.sha to the exact frozen commit and candidate.state to "frozen".

3. Re-run every required check at that SHA and record status, observed_at_sha and an evidence reference for each. A check whose underlying code changed since the last candidate may NOT be carried forward — re-run it or mark it not_run.
4. Attach owner evidence references for the live items.
5. Run `npm run launch:gate`. It recomputes both verdicts; it cannot be argued with.
6. Run `npm run launch:render` to regenerate docs/LAUNCH_STATE.md.

Any commit after step 2 that changes code creates a NEW candidate: the SHA no longer matches HEAD, every check pinned to the old SHA stops counting, and the verdict returns to NO-GO. Documentation-only commits (docs/ and the prompt packs) do not.
